evals.prompt: Write a Playwright e2e for our contact form. User opens /contact, fills name + email + message, submits, and should see a success alert. Prefer a page object.
evals.expected_output: Uses User Story → Given → When → it nesting. Given does goto/setup only; When holds the fill/submit gesture(s) in beforeEach; assertions only in it. Uses getByRole/label (or page-object wrappers), not data-testid as primary. Page object for goto/form actions. No flat 'opens and submits' it. No 'and'/'then' in describe titles.
assertions: Top-level describe starts with 'User Story:'
Uses Given → When → it nesting (not a flat single it)
Given only arrives at /contact (goto); does not perform the form fill under test
When action(s) live in beforeEach
Assertions only appear inside it/test
Queries use role/label or page-object methods, not data-testid as primary
Uses a page/screen object for goto and form interactions
No 'and' or 'then' in describe titles

evals.prompt: hey can you sketch a jest/rtl test for the login screen? user lands on it, types email/password, hits sign in, ends up on the dashboard
evals.expected_output: Triggers on casual phrasing. Same BDD nesting with Testing Library APIs: render in Given, userEvent gestures in When beforeEach, expects in it. Accessible queries (getByRole/getByLabelText). Still User Story shaped — runner change only.
assertions: Triggers on casual phrasing without requiring 'BDD' or 'Playwright'
Uses User Story → Given → When → it
Given uses render(...) for the login screen
When uses userEvent (or equivalent) in beforeEach
Uses getByRole / getByLabelText over getByTestId
Assertions only in it/test

evals.prompt: Add unit tests for formatCurrency(amount, locale) — covers en-US, nl-BE, and negative amounts.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes pure unit tests. Keeps flat describe/it. Does NOT invent User Story / Given / When nesting. May briefly note BDD nesting is for user-based UI tests only.
assertions: Treats this as a unit test of a pure helper
Uses flat describe + it only
Does not add User Story / Given / When nesting
Does not invent a fake UI flow around formatCurrency

evals.expected_output: Rewrites into User Story nesting. Splits setup vs gesture vs assert. Moves payment failure mock into Given (scenario setup), not mid-flow after a When. assertions: Rewrites into User Story → Given → When → it (or Given → it where appropriate)
Payment failure mock is registered in Given, not after a user gesture mid-test
Replaces getByTestId as primary query with role/label or page-object methods
Does not nest Given under When
Assertions stay in it only
Does not keep the flat single-it structure

evals.prompt: We're adding MSW handlers for GET /api/orders and POST /api/orders in our checkout RTL tests. Keep fixtures and handlers consistent with how we do mocks elsewhere.
evals.expected_output: Introduces MOCK_ORDER (or similar) builder with realistic defaults and overrides. Handler builders per endpoint; register mocks inside Given only. Payload verification via observation callbacks, not ad-hoc request parsing in the test body. Same builders usable beyond MSW if mentioned.
assertions: Uses a MOCK_<ENTITY> builder with defaults + overrides
Provides reusable handler builders for the order endpoints
Registers mocks inside Given, not in When/it
Verifies request payloads via observation callback (or equivalent), not inline ad-hoc parsing
Does not dump fat inline fixture objects in the spec

evals.prompt: Should I put the billing-address and payment-method checkout stories in separate test files? Each is ~200 lines today.
evals.expected_output: Applies file-organization guidance: keep related stories for the same page/feature together until ~2000 lines or a clear domain/role split. Advises against early fragmentation for two related checkout flows totaling ~400 lines.
assertions: Recommends keeping related checkout stories together for now
References the ~2000 line (or clear domain/role split) threshold
Does not push premature file splits for ~400 lines of related coverage
